recommendations.text: Integrate code review into your daily workflow. Adopt test-driven development: write failing tests first, implement until passing. Maintain regression tests to catch future breakage.
Use pull request templates that enforce code review checklists. Pair TDD with continuous integration for fast feedback.
When tests are failing, use structured debug sessions: isolate the failing assertion, add targeted logging, and bisect commit history to find regressions.
Run test suites with verbose output to surface exact failure messages. Use pytest -x to stop at the first failing test.
Use Hermes to run academic paper searches across arXiv and Semantic Scholar. A synthesis of findings from multiple sources is essential for a rigorous literature review on any research topic.
Supplement academic databases with web searches for recent preprints and grey literature.
Run market research queries to map the competitive domain. Identify key players, pricing trends, and gaps in the current market landscape.
Use DuckDuckGo to find recent news and analyst reports in your market domain for up-to-date competitive intelligence.
Use Hermes to fetch YouTube transcripts and generate concise video summary outputs from long-form content.
Batch multiple YouTube videos: extract transcripts, summarize each, and produce a cross-video summary in one session.
Set up email triage rules with Hermes: label urgent items, archive newsletters, and maintain inbox zero with daily review sessions.
Use Hermes to draft quick replies to routine inbox messages, reducing time spent on email triage significantly.
Automate calendar scheduling with Hermes: create followup reminders, block deep-work slots, and sync meeting notes automatically.
Use Hermes scheduling workflows to prevent back-to-back meetings and ensure all action items have followup tasks created.
When a deploy fails, check GitHub Actions CI logs first: identify the failing step, reproduce locally, and add a rollback step to your pipeline.
Use Hermes to trace CI failures across branches. Annotate failed GitHub Actions runs with root cause notes to prevent repeat incidents.
Combine code review and test-driven development: review pull requests against TDD criteria, ensuring each feature has passing regression tests before merge.
Supplement coding sessions with YouTube transcript summaries of conference talks on TDD and software quality.
Integrate YouTube-based learning into your code review workflow: watch transcript summaries of relevant tech talks to inform review standards.
Combine deep research with structured writing: use Hermes to retrieve sources, then apply writing skill templates to synthesize findings into publishable content.
Document research outputs using Hermes writing workflows. Build a personal skill library of domain-specific writing patterns.
Welcome to Hermes! The first setup step is writing your soul.md file — it tells Hermes who you are and how you work. Without it, Hermes can only give generic guidance.
Create soul.md with at least a Role and Workflow section. Once done, Hermes can tailor every recommendation to your specific goals.
Your soul.md is sparse — add workflow details and skills you rely on so Hermes can tailor recommendations. Describe your daily tools, routines, and any skills already installed.
Hermes can support your machine learning research goals. Use the research pipeline to find recent data papers and synthesize findings across your focus areas.
Your Zotero workflow pairs well with Hermes data ingestion: pipe annotated papers into the knowledge graph so machine learning queries surface your own prior research.
Use Hermes to plan your Python code refactor: identify high-churn modules, apply consistent naming conventions, and track technical debt as you improve code quality.
Refactor Python code incrementally: extract functions, add type annotations, and run tests after each change to confirm behavior is preserved.
